titre: The Greatest Extinction Did Not Need an Asteroid
accroche: 252 million years ago, more than nine marine species in ten disappear, with no crater, no impact. The culprit is spread over a million years.
contenu_vulgarise:
At the end of the Permian, about 252 million years ago, life on Earth goes through the most severe extinction in its history, more radical than the one that will carry off the dinosaurs 186 million years later. More than nine marine species in ten disappear, along with a majority of land species. Unlike the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary, no iridium layer and no crater signals an extraterrestrial impact at this date. The suspect identified by geologists is of a different nature: the Siberian Traps, a stack of volcanic flows that covers, in a little over a million years, a surface comparable to that of the continental United States under several kilometers of lava.

## Volcanism That Begins Before the Extinction

Beyond their volume, it is their timing that makes the Siberian Traps credible as a cause. Precise datings show that most of the volcanic activity begins about 300,000 years before the start of the extinction itself, and continues after it. This offset is not a problem for the hypothesis: it corresponds to the time needed for cumulative environmental disturbances to reach a critical threshold, as opposed to an instantaneous shock like an asteroid impact.

## A Chain of Causes, Not a Single Mechanism

As it seeps through thick sedimentary basins rich in coal and evaporites, the magma heats the rocks it passes through and releases considerable volumes of carbon dioxide, methane and sulfur compounds, a process distinct from the simple eruption of lava at the surface. A study published in 2021 also measured, in sediments dated to this period, nickel isotopes showing a signature characteristic of Siberian igneous rocks. This is an argument in favor of nickel-rich aerosols dispersed by this volcanism into the world's oceans, where they would have disrupted biological productivity and favored the appearance of oxygen-depleted marine zones. The interpretation remains debated: a scientific comment published in 2022 proposes instead a local origin for this signal, through chemical exchange with the marine sediments themselves, without transport from Siberia.

## A Slow but Complete Collapse

To this are added global warming linked to the greenhouse effect, the acidification of the oceans by dissolved carbon dioxide, and increased exposure to ultraviolet radiation if the ozone layer was damaged by volcanic emissions. None of these mechanisms taken alone explains an extinction of this magnitude; it is their accumulation over several hundred thousand years that leaves the Permian biosphere, already weakened, unable to absorb additional stress. The comparison with the extinction of the dinosaurs is direct: a brief, intense shock, or a prolonged, cumulative stress, can lead to the same catastrophic result, by entirely different paths. There is no single way to wipe 90% of marine life off the map.

repere.texte: The eruption of the Siberian Traps covers, in a little over a million years, a surface comparable to that of the continental United States, beginning about 300,000 years before the start of an extinction that eliminates more than 90% of marine species, 252 million years ago.
repere.source: MIT News, 2015; Li et al., Nature Communications, 2021

carte.punch: An extinction with no trace of an asteroid carried off more than nine marine species in ten.
carte.idee: About 252 million years ago, no crater or iridium layer signals an impact. The suspect: the Siberian Traps, volcanic flows that cover, in a little over a million years, a surface comparable to the continental United States, under several kilometers of lava.

quiz.question: Why does the 300,000-year offset between the start of the Siberian eruptions and the start of the extinction not contradict the hypothesis of a cause-and-effect link?
choix: Because the datings for this period are too imprecise to be reliable
Because environmental disturbances accumulated before reaching a critical threshold
Because the extinction actually began before the volcanic eruptions
Because the two events are not related and their simultaneity is a coincidence
quiz.explication: A cumulative environmental stress, greenhouse gases, acidification, anoxia, takes time to reach a critical threshold, unlike the instantaneous shock of an asteroid impact. This offset corresponds precisely to that accumulation time, which several independent studies on the precise chronology of the eruptions confirm.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What geologically distinguishes the Permian extinction from the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction that carried off the dinosaurs?
choix: A thick iridium layer confirms an asteroid impact identical to the Cretaceous one
A crater several hundred kilometers wide has been located in Siberia
No iridium layer and no crater signals an extraterrestrial impact at this date
The two extinctions share exactly the same carbon isotope signature
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Unlike the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary, where an iridium layer and a crater signal an asteroid impact, no trace of this kind accompanies the Permian extinction: the identified suspect is volcanic.

quiz_supplementaire.question: By what precise mechanism does the magma of the Siberian Traps release CO2, methane and sulfur compounds, as distinct from the simple eruption of lava at the surface?
choix: The magma cools abruptly on contact with the ocean, which releases large quantities of oxygen
Volcanic ash blocks sunlight for several consecutive centuries
Surface lava flows absorb atmospheric carbon dioxide as they cool
The magma seeps into sedimentary basins rich in coal and evaporites, heats these rocks and releases these gases
quiz_supplementaire.explication: As it passes through sedimentary basins rich in coal and evaporites, the magma heats these rocks and releases considerable volumes of CO2, methane and sulfur compounds, a mechanism distinct from the simple eruption of lava at the surface.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the 2022 scientific comment propose as an alternative explanation for the nickel isotope signature found in the sediments?
choix: Contamination of the samples by modern nickel-steel drilling tools
A local origin of the signal, through chemical exchange with the marine sediments themselves, without transport from Siberia
An extraterrestrial origin of the nickel, brought by a shower of micrometeorites
A displacement of the signal by ocean currents coming from the present-day Pacific Ocean
quiz_supplementaire.explication: A 2022 scientific comment proposes that the nickel isotope signal is explained by a local chemical exchange with marine sediments, rather than by transport of aerosols from Siberia, leaving the interpretation debated.
